explanations.text:
●  the map command lives in this file
│     When you ask the tool to save an abstraction, everything
│     below happens here. The shared machinery — the pieces of
│     a file, [the checking of every pin](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:build_anchors) —
│     lives in [the tool's main file](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py), and this
│     file asks it for those steps.
│
●  the tool picks up what is abstracted already            ([load_map](load_map))
│     In the project's human folder sits a second file. It
│     holds every abstraction written so far. On the first
│     run it is empty.
│
●  the tool finds the lines the abstraction covers      ([entry_span](entry_span))
│     An abstraction can cover the whole file or one named piece.
│     Here the tool notes the first and the last line of what
│     it covers. A name that is not in the file stops the run.
│
●  the tool numbers the abstraction                          ([next_id](next_id))
│     The first one it ever saved is number 1, the next is
│     number 2, and so on. The new one gets the next number.
│     The number is how you point at it later: you say
│     "reword number 3", and the tool knows which one you mean.
│
●  the second file grows                                     ([cmd_map](cmd_map))
│     With the abstraction, the tool saves three things:
│         the words, exactly as written
│         the pins inside those words
│         for each pin, the lines of code it points at
│     Then the tool reads the whole file once more and counts
│     the lines of code that no abstraction points at yet.
│     It writes all of this into the second file — the record
│     in the project's human folder; for cmd_map.py it is named
│     explanation_compiler__cli__human__cmd_map.py.json. The
│     code file itself is never touched. Then the tool tells
│     you what it saved and how many lines are still bare.
│
●  a whole project can carry one abstraction          ([map_project](map_project))
      When you point the tool at a folder instead of a file,
      the abstraction goes into human/human.json at the
      project root. It has no lines of its own. Its pins point
      at the files of the project — one line per file, what
      the file is for. A pin that points anywhere else stops
      the run.
